findings:
🟠 [guard-warn-name-set-only] MUST-FIX `ts_guard_after` in hooks/tests/lib/test-snapshot.sh builds its refs/worktrees/status warnings from name sets only (`_ts_ref_names`, `_ts_worktree_paths`, `_ts_status_paths` fed to `comm -3`), so a change that keeps the same name prints nothing. Concrete failure: a child that commits on the real repo's current branch moves `refs/heads/<branch>` to a new sha; `cmp` sees the for-each-ref files differ, but the name sets are identical, `_ts_warn_names` gets an empty list and returns silently. The same happens for a status code change on an existing path (` M` to `M `) and a worktree whose HEAD or branch changes. Impact: the most likely real-repo write (a commit on the real branch) produces no WARNING, against G6 and the spec's "print a WARNING line naming what differs (the names of the changed refs or paths)". Smallest remediation: run `comm -3` on the sorted full before/after lines, then extract and `sort -u` the names from the differing lines, so the name is still the only thing printed; add one case that moves an existing ref and asserts the WARNING names it.
🟠 [guard-slash-key-dropped] MUST-FIX `_ts_explode_config_z` uses the raw config key as a filename (`printf '%s\0' "$val" >>"$dir/$key"`), but subsection keys can legally contain `/` (`url.https://host/.insteadof`, `http.https://github.com/.extraheader`, `submodule.a/b.url`, `lfs.<url>.access`). Concrete failure: after a child runs `git config --local url.https://example.com/.insteadOf x`, the redirect fails with "No such file or directory", the key is never recorded, and `ts_guard_after` returns 0 with no DRIFT line and no restore. Impact: config drift on any such key goes undetected, against "for every key whose value set changed, was added, or was removed". If the real repo's baseline already has such a key, every no-change run prints shell errors, against "no-change ... prints nothing". Smallest remediation: encode the key into a safe filename (e.g. escape `%` then `/`, or numbered files plus a key index) and decode it for the DRIFT line and the restore; add one case with a slash-containing key.
🔵 [guard-valueless-key-restore] CUT/FOLLOW-UP A valueless key (`[core] foo` with no `=`, listed by `-z` as `core.foo\0`) falls into the `=` fallback in `_ts_explode_config_z`, so its stored value is the key name. Comparison stays consistent, but a restore would write `core.foo=core.foo`. Excluded: it needs a child to modify a valueless boolean key, and no spec case covers it.
🔵 [guard-before-list-failure] CUT/FOLLOW-UP If `git config --local --list -z` fails in `ts_guard_before`, it is swallowed by `|| true` and the snapshot is empty, so `ts_guard_after` would treat every real key as added and `--unset-all` it. Excluded: it needs the listing to fail on a valid repo root, and failing closed on an unreadable baseline is hardening the spec does not ask for.
